name: Morse.IsRelCellAttachment
difference: The project's predicate is literal: K must be the iterated pushout and j the composite of the cellInl's. The blind one is only up to a homeomorphism of K compatible with the map. Example with no cells: not : Bool → Bool satisfies the blind notion (it is a homeomorphism) but not the project's, which forces j = 𝟙. Exactly: T L K f ds ⟺ ∃ K' j (e : K' ≅ K), P L K' j ds ∧ j ≫ e.hom = f.
why: P ⇒ T outright (P_imp_T), and T is exactly the closure of P under homeomorphisms of the target compatible with the maps (agree). The proof uses blind Quot adjunction space ≅ project pushout, invariance of the pushout under homeomorphism of the base, and snoc/unsnoc lemmas converting head-first recursion into the project's tail-first induction. The rigidity is a modelling convention ("obtained from" read as the literal pushout). The project uses the predicate only in conclusions and inside existentials (CellTower), so it is harmless.
